ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $CD \perp AB$ with the foot of the perpendicular as D. If $AD = 2$ and $BD = 4$, then what is the length of $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In the right $\triangle ACB$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $CD\perp AB$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACD=\angle B=90^\circ-\angle A$,\\
Also, $\because \angle ACD=\angle CDB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ACD\sim \triangle CBD$,\\
$\therefore CD^2=AD\cdot BD=8$, that is $CD=\boxed{2\sqrt{2}}$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a right triangle ABC with C at the top, A and B on the bottom line, and D on segment AB where the altitude CD meets AB. From the text, use ∠ACB = 90°, CD ⟂ AB, AD = 2, and BD = 4. Apply the right-triangle altitude-to-hypotenuse theorem: for an altitude from the right angle to the hypotenuse, the altitude length satisfies CD^2 = AD · BD. Thus CD^2 = 2 · 4 = 8, so CD = 2√2.
